notes: MKR Vidor 4000 is not in the catalogue, so a new part type was created; its pin labels follow the diagram (pin 'DAC0/A0' is named A0).

The diagram's breadboard is drawn with row letters j..f in the upper half and e..a in the lower half (flipped relative to the catalogue's 't' = a-e). I used the diagram's row letters with the 'b' bank (rows f-j) for the upper half, where all parts sit.

Resistor legs read from the image at columns 3 and 6 (row h); the green wire goes to column 3 (row g) and the LED legs go into columns 6 and 8 (row i). The black wire ends at column 8 (row h). The bent (longer) LED leg at column 6 is treated as the anode.
The LED is driven from pin 2 through the 82 ohm resistor and returns to GND (the sketch uses ledPin = 2).
The Library Manager screenshot and the software steps (WiFiNINA, VidorPeripherals) add no physical parts. A USB cable to power/program the board is implied but not shown, so it is not included.
